sense: of weather, pain or hardship: harsh, hard to bear

evidence: Plaut. Men. 5.2.119: morbum ācrem ac dūrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sharp and piercing: a sharp winter (Ennius, Horace), sharp pain, hunger, thirst (Lewis & Short). Its main senses are sharp, keen, eager: of a person it means keen or fierce, not strict (see severe, of a person). For a severe illness or wound the usual word is gravis (see serious).
Hard to bear: the hardest time of the year, hard pains, hard poverty (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Tac. G. 2: aspera caelō, harsh in climate (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rough to the touch, and so rough and harsh: a rough sea, a harsh winter, a harsh country.

phrases.latin: Solvitur ācris hiems grātā vice vēris et Favōnī
phrases.english: harsh winter is loosening its grip as spring and the west wind come round in welcome turn

phrases.latin: mōns Cevenna … dūrissimō tempore annī altissimā nive iter impediēbat
phrases.english: at the hardest time of the year the Cévennes blocked the way with very deep snow

sources: Lewis & Short: acer · Lewis & Short: durus · Lewis & Short: asper
